item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q021_nad_binding_convergent_evolution","answer":"The occurrence of NAD/NADP-dependent enzymes in several SCOPe folds and superfamilies means that “binds NAD(P)” is not evidence for one NAD(P)-enzyme ancestor. Within a SCOPe family, and often within a SCOPe superfamily, the shared cofactor site is part of a homologous structural core and can reflect divergent evolution after duplication. Across different SCOPe superfamilies, and especially across different folds, the same redox cofactor has been recruited independently: these are convergent or analogous solutions to binding a chemically useful dinucleotide. A representative Rossmann example is the SCOP fold c.2, NAD(P)-binding Rossmann-fold domains, in the alpha/beta class; unrelated NAD(P)-binding enzymes also occur outside that fold, so the cofactor is a functional descriptor, not a homology boundary. Cofactor binding or active-site resemblance alone is insufficient because NAD(P) imposes recurring local requirements: phosphate/ribose recognition, glycine-rich loops, helix-dipole interactions, and placement of a nicotinamide ring next to a hydride donor or acceptor. Those local motifs and catalytic geometries can arise on different beta-sheet topologies and in different domain architectures. SCOPe superfamily assignment therefore requires evidence from the whole-domain fold, topology, conserved structural core, sequence motifs in context, and characteristic residue geometry; a shared small-molecule ligand, an Enzyme Commission reaction, or a visually similar catalytic pocket is unsafe by itself. Consequently, function transfer, homology claims, and template choice should be restricted to the appropriate SCOPe family or well-supported superfamily unless independent whole-structure and sequence evidence connects the proteins; a fold-level or class-level match should be treated only as a possible structural template relationship, not proof of common ancestry or detailed active-site equivalence.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
